པར་འགྱུར་བ་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་དག་ཡོད་པ་མ་ཡིན་པས། །འབྲས་བུ་བཞི་ཡང་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །འབྲས་བུ་མེད་ན་འབྲས་གནས་མེད། །ཞུགས་པ་དག་ཀྱང་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །གལ་ཏེ་སྐྱེས་བུ་གང་ཟག་བརྒྱད། །དེ་དག་མེད་ན་དགེ་འདུན་མེད། །འཕགས་པའི་
བདེན་རྣམས་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར། །དམ་པའི་ཆོས་ཀྱང་ཡོད་མ་ཡིན། །ཆོས་དང་དགེ་འདུན་ཡོད་མིན་ན། །སངས་རྒྱས་ཇི་ལྟར་ཡོད་པར་འགྱུར། །དེ་སྐད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་སྨྲ་ན། །དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་ལ་གནོད་པ་ནི། །བྱེད་ཅིང་འབྲས་བུ་ཡོད་པ་དང་། །ཆོས་མ་ཡིན་པ་#
ཆོས་ཉིད་དང་། །འཇིག་རྟེན་པ་ཡི་ཐ་སྙད་ནི། །ཀུན་ལའང་གནོད་པ་བྱེད་པ་ཡིན། །དེ་ལ་བཤད་པ་ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་ནི། །སྟོང་ཉིད་དགོས་དང་སྟོང་ཉིད་དང་། །སྟོང་ཉིད་དོན་ནི་མ་རྟོགས་པས། །དེ་ཕྱིར་དེ་ལྟར་གནོད་པ་ཡིན། །སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཆོས་བསྟན་པ། །

In [that which is empty], how could it exist? If a self, purity, permanence, and happiness existed, then self, purity, permanence, and happiness would not be subversions. If a self, purity, permanence, and happiness do not exist, then selflessness, impurity, impermanence, and suffering do not exist either. Thus, by the ceasing of subversions, ignorance comes to cease. When ignorance has ceased, then karmic formations and the rest will cease. If some mental afflictions existed by their own nature, how could they ever be abandoned? Who can abandon what is inherently existent? If some mental afflictions did not exist by their own nature, how could they ever be abandoned? Who can abandon what is non-existent? This was the twenty-third chapter, titled "The Investigation of Subversions."

If all these things are empty, there would be no arising and no perishing. It would follow that for you, the four noble truths do not exist. Since the four noble truths would not exist, then thorough knowledge <note>of suffering</note>, abandonment <note>of the origin</note>, meditation <note>on the path</note>, and realization <note>of cessation</note> would not be tenable. Since those things would not exist, the four fruits <note>of the spiritual life: stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner, and arhat</note> would also not exist. If the fruits do not exist, those who abide in the fruits do not exist, and those who enter the paths do not exist. If the eight types of persons <note>the four pairs of those entering and abiding in the four fruits</note> do not exist, then the Sangha <gloss>Spiritual Community</gloss> does not exist. Because the noble truths do not exist, the Sublime Dharma <gloss>Teachings</gloss> also does not exist. If the Dharma and the Sangha do not exist, how could a Buddha exist? By speaking thus of emptiness, you negate the Three Jewels, and you negate the existence of results, the nature of things that are not the Dharma, and all worldly conventions. To this we say: because you do not understand the purpose of emptiness, emptiness itself, and the meaning of emptiness, you are harmed by these views. The teaching of the Dharma by the Buddhas
tail: is perfectly based upon two truths: the worldly relative truth <note>original: "samvrti-satya"</note> and the ultimate truth <note>original: "paramartha-satya"</note>.
old_translation:
...one who is subverted?

If a self, purity, permanence, and happiness existed, then the self, purity, permanence, and happiness would not be subversions <note>they would be true</note>.

If a self, purity, permanence, and happiness do not exist, then selfless, impure, impermanent, and suffering do not exist either.

Thus, by the cessation of subversion, ignorance ceases. When ignorance has ceased, the formations and the rest <note>the twelve links of dependent origination</note> cease.

If someone's mental afflictions existed by inherent nature, how could they be abandoned? Who could abandon what inherently exists?

If someone's mental afflictions did not exist by inherent nature <note>meaning they were utterly non-existent</note>, how could they be abandoned? Who could abandon what does not exist?

This was the twenty-third chapter, titled "Examination of the Subversions."

If all these are empty, there is no arising and no perishing. It would follow for you that the four noble truths do not exist.

If the four noble truths do not exist, then thorough knowledge <note>of suffering</note>, abandoning <note>of the origin</note>, meditation <note>on the path</note>, and realization <note>of cessation</note> are not possible.

If those do not exist, the four fruits <note>stages of enlightenment</note> also do not exist. If the fruits do not exist, those who abide in the fruits do not exist, nor do those who enter the paths.

If those eight types of persons do not exist, then the <term>Sangha</term> <gloss>the spiritual community</gloss> does not exist. Because the noble truths do not exist, the holy <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>the teachings</gloss> also does not exist.

If the Dharma and the Sangha do not exist, how could the Buddha exist? By speaking of emptiness in that way, you cause harm to the Three Jewels.

You also cause harm to the reality of the fruits, the distinction between what is not Dharma and what is Dharma, and all worldly conventions.

To this we say: You have not understood the purpose of emptiness, emptiness itself, or the meaning of emptiness. Therefore, you see harm in it where there is none.

The teaching of the Dharma by the Buddhas...

<summary>This page concludes the analysis of subversions and introduces the twenty-fourth chapter. It presents an opponent's objection that if everything is empty, then the fundamental tenets of Buddhism—the Four Noble Truths and the Three Jewels—would be destroyed.</summary>
